subject: bicycle
pitch: A vintage Dutch city bicycle in mint green. Tall upright handlebars with cream grips and a silver bell, a brown leather saddle with springs, chrome mudguards, a chain guard, a wicker basket on the front filled with sunflowers and a baguette, and whitewall tyres.
reasoning:
I need to design this as a single TypeScript module requiring at least one root joint, so I'm planning a frame joint as root with additional joints for the front/rear wheels, steering, and pedal crank, then working out the overall dimensions like wheelbase.

Now I'm figuring out the geometry: rear and front axle positions, bottom bracket placement, and a step-through frame with a curved top tube connecting the head tube to the seat tube. I'm placing the head tube and fork angle so the front wheel sits correctly, making the steering joint a child of root at the head tube base, with the fork, handlebar stem, and front wheel joint attached beneath it. I'm deciding to always pass the bone explicitly when building rods for clarity, and now I'm starting on the wheel geometry using a torus shape for the tires.

Writing whitewall tire geometry...

Geometric approach for a separate ring is getting fiddly, so instead I'll just paint the whitewall directly on the tire's torus surface — computing radial distance from the wheel axis and checking the surface normal to decide where the sidewall band is cream versus black, rather than modeling it as separate geometry.

For the rim I'll use a chrome torus plus spokes modeled as thin rods radiating from hub to rim, around 32 per wheel for both wheels, staying well within the part budget.

Adding spoke geometry and hub cylinder...

Now for the mudguards I'm thinking of sweeping a flattened cross-section along an arc path centered on the wheel, with the radius function shaping it to hug the tire curvature.

Working out fender geometry to a 140-degree sweep, anchoring the front fender at the steer joint and rear fender at the root. I'm sizing the box-section radii (0.05 sideways, 0.005 thin) so the fender cross-section rides correctly in the YZ arc plane, with width along X as the binormal. I'll add rod stays connecting fenders to the axle and go with chrome fenders over the mint frame, maybe a small red reflector detail.

Now I'm placing the main frame geometry: mint tubes at 0.016 radius, with the bottom bracket, rear axle, leaning seat tube, chainstays and seatstays splitting around the rear axle at x=±0.06, and the head tube and fork positioned to connect the steering joint down to the front axle.

Working out fork leg positions near the axle, then shaping the main curved tube for a Dutch step-through frame using a catmull-rom spline from the head tube down through the bottom bracket area to the seat tube.

I'll skip a second upper tube and keep just the single swooping frame tube. Now I'm placing the steering joint at the head tube top with an axis tilted along the head angle, adding a quill stem that rises and sets back to support swept-back Dutch-style handlebars centered above the steerer.

I'm curving the bars outward and back using a spline for each side, reaching upright grip positions with a thicker swept tube radius for the grip ends.

Now I'm adding a silver bell on the left bar with a domed hemisphere and striker button, plus small black brake lever rods extending from each grip, and placing a chrome headlight lamp on the fork crown attached to the steering assembly.

I'm also positioning a wicker front basket pushed forward of the handlebars to avoid overlap, sized around 0.38 wide, 0.28 deep, 0.24 tall, sitting above the fender top with support rods running down to the fork axle.

Building woven texture...

For the rim and handles, I'll use rod sweeps forming a square rim plus curved arc handles on the sides positioned above the basket. For contents, I'm planning sunflower stems rising from inside the basket to flower heads, each flower built from a dark brown center disc surrounded by a ring of yellow petal shapes facing outward and up.

I need a flower function that generates a center cylinder plus a ring of spike-shaped petals around it, but I'm realizing the frame's bone attachment is tricky since the nearest joint (steer) has no children, which could give it a zero-length bone. I should probably add a child joint for the basket to give petals a proper bone reference.

Given the complexity of ring-with-frame, maybe I'll skip that helper and construct petals manually instead, computing a perpendicular basis for the direction vector by hand and looping through each petal angle to place spikes as outward-pointing cones from the basket joint. It's stylized but should look reasonably flower-like.

I'm planning two staggered petal layers in orange-yellow and yellow tones, then positioning five sunflower heads along stems rising from the basket, each angled slightly differently so they face forward and upward with enough spacing to avoid overlap.

Still positioning the baguette...

Now for the saddle, I'm thinking leather brown with a Brooks-style loft shape, mounted on the seat post, wide Dutch-style with a length of about 0.28 running from the rear to the nose.

Still placing spring and seat geometry...

Closing the bridge rod back to the seat post, then moving to the rear rack: positioning a Dutch-style carrier platform over the rear fender, figuring its height and span relative to the wheel and fender geometry, and laying out the side rails and cross bars connecting to the axle stays.

Now I'm designing the chain guard as a full Dutch-style chaincase on the right side, using an extruded outline that curves from the chainring area near the bottom bracket to the rear hub, giving it a rounded capsule silhouette in side view.

Plotting outline coordinates...

I'm checking the chaincase shape isn't self-intersecting and settling on a mint color matching the frame with slight thickness, plus a chrome crank cap. Now I'm setting up the crank and pedal structure, jointed at the bottom bracket axle with arms extending to pedal positions on each side.

Pedal centers settle at x ±0.17. For the wheel joints, I'm placing rearWheel and frontWheel with spin axis along X so rotation about local Y produces the hinge motion, keeping joints simple as single children rather than chains. I'm setting the root frame joint near the BB position to anchor the whole skeleton.

For the kickstand, I'm positioning a rod from the chainstay down to near the floor so its lowest point just touches ground level, adding a small foot contact at the bottom.

Working out the whitewall band radii using the torus angle math, then checking the hub cylinder dimensions for the wheel rotation.

I realize I need to orient the torus geometry correctly since it defaults to axis Y but I want axis Z with a direction vector, and I'm thinking through how the paint function uses model-space normals so the whitewall band gets applied properly per-face with flat shading across the 8 radial segments.

Switching to 12 segments with a 15° offset gives better normal thresholds (sin 45° and 75° both exceed 0.5) so the whitewall paint falls on the correct faces on both sides, while keeping flat shading for the stylized look. I'll total up the part count across spokes and other components to stay under budget, and figure out the color palette needed.

For the tire paint, I'm writing a function that takes position and normal and returns a color string based on radial distance. I'm also working out where to place a front lamp — the head tube seems safer than the fork crown since the crown position collides with the fender and basket geometry.

Dropping the lamp idea, I'll add red and white reflectors instead. I'm calculating the angular placement on the rear fender curve to position a red reflector near its trailing end, working through the trig for y and z coordinates at different theta values to avoid overlap with the fender body.

I'm also adding a bell on the handlebar with a silver dome and base, then working out the head tube, stem, and handlebar geometry for a tall Dutch-style upright position, defining the rod positions and clamp joints along the steering axis.

Checking the basket joint position relative to the steer axis, and verifying the floor clearance—tire bottoms sit at y=0 with the kickstand as the lowest point, so wheel radii and centers need to line up correctly. I'm considering whether to add small rivet spheres along the saddle's rear edge for detail, but deciding to skip them and just use color/shading on the leather instead.

I'm now applying a mottled leather paint to the saddle for texture, then moving to the frame tubes—using sweep operations along catmull paths bound to the root bone for the main structure. For the seat tube and other rods connecting the bottom bracket to the seat area, I'm switching to capsule shapes instead of flat-capped rods so the joints look smoother, and planning chrome ring details at the headset using cylinders at the top and bottom of the head tube.

For the fenders, I'm working out the arc geometry—computing start angles and rotation axes so the front fender curves from roughly -50° around to near the axle level, and the rear fender sweeps from about -105° through 140° to wrap properly around the wheel.

Now I'm adding tapered chrome support stays connecting each fender to its axle hub, using a radius array to give them a slight linear taper for a more realistic rod shape.

I'm placing the rear reflector as a small red cylinder near the fender end around (0,0.285,-0.96), then defining the chainstays and seatstays as capsules running from the bottom bracket and seat tube out to the rear axle.

Checking the seatstay geometry, I notice it passes close to the rear tire's surface near y=0.6 — the clearance is tight, maybe slightly clashing, so I'm widening the stay position outward in x toward the axle to avoid the tire intersection.

Working through clearances between fork legs, fender width, chainstays, and tire edges, settling on fork legs at x≈0.06 and fender half-width at 0.048 so everything clears properly, then shifting to building a function that constructs sunflower petal shapes using vector math in THREE.js, normalizing a direction vector and computing a perpendicular helper vector.

Writing petal spike generation...

Now I'm working out the stems as green capsules running from the basket up to each flower head, with a couple leaf spikes angled off the sides for texture. Then I'm starting on the basket itself, building its walls as boxes parented to a steer joint bone.

Adding wicker pattern...

For the rim, I'll sweep a thin closed polyline around the top corners using darker wicker color. For the interior, I'm thinking a gingham checker cloth draped over the basket—a thin slab in red/white checker paint sitting inside near the top edge, letting the stems pass through it so it looks naturally filled.

Now I'm adding a baguette poking through the cloth, positioning its endpoints so it clears the front wall and rim without intersecting geometry.

Adjusting the dome geometry with an open bottom so the base cylinder covers the seam, then moving to the brake levers—plotting chrome rod positions along the handlebar path from grip to lever tip.

Mirroring the handlebars left-right using the path points, then working on the fork geometry—figuring out the crown rod position connecting the steerer to the head tube, and the leg capsules running down from the crown to the axle at a matching slope.

I'm skipping extra details like dress guards and checking where the down tube meets the head tube axis, calculating the z-offset along the head tube's slight angle to get the junction point right.

Now I'm positioning the kickstand as a chrome rod running from the chainstay down to a foot near ground level, working out the capsule endpoints and radius so it reads as a thin cylindrical leg touching down just above zero.

I'm layering in finishing details: a pedal box, chain guard cap, small front reflector, and a Dutch-style ring lock (black box with chrome shackle) mounted near the rear seat stays where they bridge the fender, figuring out placement so it sits properly against the fender top without clipping the wheel.

That position clears the fender arc with margin, so I'll size the lock box small and skip the shackle detail, just adding a simple dark box with a small chrome ring and silver cylinder cap for the key. Now I'm setting up helper functions for capsules and planning the spoke assembly for each wheel joint.

Writing spoke geometry...

Adding a crank joint at the same position as the root, which should be fine, then moving to pedals and paint colors as string values. Now I'm working out the sunflower placement data, computing stem base positions relative to each flower's pos and running a capsule-shaped rod from base to flower, checking that the stems pass near the basket's front rim correctly.

Then I'm adding leaf spikes branching off each stem partway up, all bound to the basket bone, followed by a curved handle swept across the basket using catmull points on either side, and setting the rim height and wall dimensions for the basket itself.

Checking the rack rods connecting basket mounts down to the fender and axle area, making sure the rod radius and positions clear the tire and fender geometry without collisions, then confirming the basket is parented to the steering joint so it turns with the handlebars. Now finalizing the code structure and imports needed for the build.
